<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אדר_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917370_theRebbe_643" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_93_D7_A8_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917370_theRebbe_643__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the opening header and date for the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Tuesday,</t>
    <t s="2">Purim Katan 5738*.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the paradox that in the time of the Purim exile, the Jews fulfilled what they had already accepted at the Giving of the Torah, a matter of "wondrous" transcendence beyond all comparison.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"And the Jews accepted that which they had begun to do"1,</t>
    <t s="1">and it is explained in this by my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe, our leader, in his well-known maamar2</t>
    <t s="2">which he said on Purim Katan</t>
    <t s="3">(5687)</t>
    <t s="4">in Moscow</t>
    <t s="5">[which this year is the beginning of the Jubilee3</t>
    <t s="6">second4</t>
    <t s="7">of its recitation]</t>
    <t s="8">that now, in the time of exile, they accepted what they had already begun at the time of the Giving of the Torah.</t>
    <t s="9">And as the words of our Sages, of blessed memory5,</t>
    <t s="10">on the verse6</t>
    <t s="11">"They fulfilled and accepted the Jews, etc.",</t>
    <t s="12">that they fulfilled now</t>
    <t s="13">(in the days of Achashverosh)</t>
    <t s="14">what they had already accepted at the time of the Giving of the Torah.</t>
    <t s="15">And he precisely notes in this maamar,</t>
    <t s="16">that at first glance it is a wondrous thing</t>
    <t s="17">[and he precisely notes in his question that this is a matter of "wondrous"</t>
    <t s="18">(and not like the usual language in most maamarim – "it needs to be understood")</t>
    <t s="19">because the matter</t>
    <t s="20">(that they accepted in the time of exile what they had begun at the time of the Giving of the Torah)</t>
    <t s="21">is in the aspect of wondrous.</t>
    <t s="22">And as explained7</t>
    <t s="23">regarding the matter of "It is not wondrous... and not distant"8,</t>
    <t s="24">that distance and closeness are relative to each other,</t>
    <t s="25">but "wondrous" indicates a matter of separation and distinction, even to the point that it is in the aspect of "wonder" relative to it,</t>
    <t s="26">and this means it is a matter that is entirely incomparable.</t>
    <t s="27">And as is known9</t>
    <t s="28">(regarding the Sefiros)</t>
    <t s="29">that the aspect of "wonder" is the aspect of Kesser,</t>
    <t s="30">and in particular, the aspect of the innerness of Kesser,</t>
    <t s="31">which is entirely beyond comprehension in relation to the entire order of the chain of descent.</t>
    <t s="32">And from this it will be understood also regarding the matter of the wondrous mentioned in the maamar],</t>
    <t s="33">that at the Giving of the Torah</t>
    <t s="34">(when they began to do)</t>
    <t s="35">the Jewish people were at the ultimate level of elevation and in a most praiseworthy state and condition,</t>
    <t s="36">and it was then after the Splitting of the Sea and the Exodus from Egypt,</t>
    <t s="37">which are matters that established each and every Jew and the entirety of the Jewish people in a most elevated state,</t>
    <t s="38">for in the Exodus from Egypt, the King of Kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed Himself upon them in His glory and redeemed them,</t>
    <t s="39">and at the time of the Splitting of the Sea</t>
    <t s="40">[which is the conclusion and seal of the Exodus from Egypt10]</t>
    <t s="41">a maidservant saw at the sea what the prophets did not see11,</t>
    <t s="42">and certainly the ultimate elevation of the Jewish people at the time of the Giving of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="43">for the Giving of the Torah was only once, as is known12</t>
    <t s="44">that the Giving of the Torah will not occur again,</t>
    <t s="45">and it is also explained in Tanya13</t>
    <t s="46">that at the time of the Giving of the Torah there was already a semblance of the ultimate perfection of the world that will be in the future,</t>
    <t s="47">which was a revelation of G-dliness in tangible sight,</t>
    <t s="48">that due to these revelations the Jewish people were at the ultimate level.</t>
    <t s="49">In contrast, in the time of exile it is the exact opposite,</t>
    <t s="50">that the Jewish people are at the lowest point of descent.</t>
    <t s="51">And especially in the time of Haman</t>
    <t s="52">(when "And the Jews accepted, etc., they fulfilled, etc." occurred)</t>
    <t s="53">who sought, Heaven forbid, to destroy, kill, and annihilate all the Jews, from youth to elder, infants and women, in one day, etc.14,</t>
    <t s="54">for this decree was most severe, as it was all at once upon all the Jews throughout the entire world,</t>
    <t s="55">for Achashverosh ruled over the entire globe, as stated in the Midrash15,</t>
    <t s="56">and it was impossible to escape to a place that was already after the decree, since it was in one day</t>
    <t s="57">(throughout the entire world),</t>
    <t s="58">which is</t>
    <t s="59">(within the exile itself)</t>
    <t s="60">the most terrible exile.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the core of Haman's decree was against Jewish education, targeting the young children, which requires mesirus nefesh to protect and establish them in their proper place.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it is explained in the maamar there that the force of</t>
    <t s="1">(the decree and)</t>
    <t s="2">the exile in spirituality was the decree regarding the matter of education.</t>
    <t s="3">And as stated in the Midrash16</t>
    <t s="4">[Haman] said</t>
    <t s="5">(Haman)</t>
    <t s="6">"I will not send my hand first except upon these children."</t>
    <t s="7">And this means that in order to carry out, Heaven forbid, his evil plot and wicked thought which he thought against the Jews, may G-d have mercy, to destroy them17,</t>
    <t s="8">the beginning is with these children of the study hall.</t>
    <t s="9">For the intention in this is the decree upon the entirety of the matter of education,</t>
    <t s="10">and it can be said that even though in the above "young students" refers to a child in years, but analogous to this is also a child in matters of Judaism,</t>
    <t s="11">even if he is an adult in years, and in the language of my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe, "he already has white hair",</t>
    <t s="12">nevertheless, in his state regarding matters of Torah and mitzvos he is in the aspect of a child.</t>
    <t s="13">[And from this very fact</t>
    <t s="14">(that the existence of the Jewish people depends on education)</t>
    <t s="15">one understands the greatness of the self-sacrifice that must be for the education of the Jewish people.</t>
    <t s="16">For one must give his soul so that "Do not touch My anointed ones"18</t>
    <t s="17">refers to these children of the study hall, as stated in Tractate Shabbos19,</t>
    <t s="18">which is accomplished by bringing the children to their proper place,</t>
    <t s="19">to the study hall,</t>
    <t s="20">and there itself, the manner of education is in a manner of "house</t>
    <t s="21">(of study)</t>
    <t s="22">" and permanent,</t>
    <t s="23">meaning that the children will receive from their teacher the foundation</t>
    <t s="24">(the entire structure)</t>
    <t s="25">for all the days of their lives].</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
